input.quote: If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer of 15% of annual Fees for each week an invoice is unpaid, triggered by a ten-day payment delay. That is a Customer-payable liquidated damages sum with no cap; within seven weeks it exceeds a full year's Fees and can exceed the remaining contract value, and it is triggered by a minor breach (short payment delay) — walk-away territory under this rule, and well beyond the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees). No early-termination fee exists elsewhere (Section 9.4 requires only accrued Fees), so this is not a double flag. Redline replaces the LD with ordinary interest on undisputed overdue amounts, reaching the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment; replace with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, particularly at 15% of annual Fees per week, which is uncapped and would quickly exceed the contract value. We have replaced it with ordinary interest on undisputed overdue amounts, consistent with the dispute mechanism in Section 7.3.

ops.oldText: If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: If any proper, undisputed invoice is not paid within thirty days of its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until payment. Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar sum.
